whatWorks: The recursion is real and legible, not decorative: at 256px seeds 5003, 5920 and 6444 show genuine self-similar generations nesting inward at diminishing scale, and the figure always reads as one centred object rather than as scattered incident.

The market amplitude is genuinely visible at browse size. On 5134, 5265 and 5396 the stress frame is unmistakable against neutral even on the 120px sheet, which is the hard part; the transformation has real reach and only needs redirecting, never reducing.

Seeds 5789 (a bare diamond inside a hexagon) and 6182 (one wide ring with a few small satellites) prove the generator can already produce sparse, open, low-ink figures with almost no mass in them. The light end of the range exists and is the end the brief actually asked for.
Every seed keeps a clean centred anchor with the figure whole and uncropped in eleven of twelve tiles, so the centred-radiating identity anchor is holding across the set.

findings.whatFails: Every seed carries a solid black filled mass at its centre - a filled disc on 5134 and 6051, a filled hexagon on 5265, 5527, 6313 and 6444 - and the bone outline around it is a wide ribbon roughly 6px at 512 (about 1.2% of canvas). At 512 the hexagon edge is the single heaviest, highest-contrast thing in the frame.
findings.why: The brief says in as many words: nothing heavy, nothing solid, no filled mass anywhere, contrast kept low so the lines read as thread rather than as structure. The medium is 'drawn entirely in outline'. A filled black core with a thick bone band around it is the exact opposite object - it reads as a cast metal seal, not as filigree.
findings.specificChange: Remove every fill: set fill to none on the core disc, the core polygon and the satellite rings so the figure is outline only, and narrow the bone stroke from ~1.2% of canvas width down to 0.3-0.4% (about 2px at 512), so the darkest pixel in the frame belongs to the ground and never to the figure.
findings.keep: The nested three-ring cluster sitting inside the core is currently the only place the recursion resolves at 512 - keep those members, their count and their spacing exactly, and simply unfill them rather than deleting the innermost generation along with the mass.

findings.whatFails: The ground is a warm sepia-olive radial gradient with a heavy dark vignette in the corners, identical in all twelve tiles, and it sits at mid value - lighter than the figure it surrounds. The dark in these images is inside the artwork; the ground is the pale part.
findings.why: The palette intent is bone and pale slate over a dark ground, and the medium calls for a flat ground. This is warm where the brief says cool, mid-value where it says dark, and gradient-plus-vignette where it says flat. The value order is inverted, which is why the lines cannot read as thread: pale thread needs dark behind it.
findings.specificChange: Replace the radial gradient and vignette with one flat uniform cool near-black slate painted edge to edge (roughly #14171B to #1B1F24), and lift the linework onto it as bone and pale slate, inverting the current value order so the figure is the light element and the ground is the dark one.
findings.keep: The low overall contrast must survive the inversion - do not answer a dark ground with pure white lines. Bone should sit only a few steps above the ground, and the blue-slate secondary should stay as the cooler, quieter of the two line colours.

findings.whatFails: The figure is a small medallion occupying roughly 35-45% of the frame width with a wide dead margin of empty gradient around it (clearest on the 512 single and on 5265, 5789, 6313). Nothing extends outward. Where reach does happen it is a failure of the opposite kind: 6051's large circles are cut flat by the left and bottom edges. Successive generations do not thin - the outermost blue-slate ring is as thick as or thicker than the inner members.
findings.why: Composition asks for a figure that reaches out toward the frame without touching it, and rhythm asks that each generation reach further and thin as it goes outward. A centred medallion in a big empty margin is not reach - the negative space is inert surround rather than space threads extend into - and constant stroke weight outward removes the only cue that says fragility increases with distance.
findings.specificChange: Grow the outermost generation until the figure's extent reaches 85-90% of frame width while stopping short of the edge, halve the stroke width at each successive generation from the centre outward so the outer members are the faintest in the frame, and clamp the figure's bounding box inside the viewBox so 6051's circles are no longer cut by the left and bottom edges.
findings.keep: The centred anchor and the untouched margin - the figure must still be centred and must still not touch or bleed off the frame. Fixing the clipping by cropping tighter, or fixing the reach by letting members run off the edge, would each break the other.

findings.whatFails: Reach is maximal under STRESS in all four state rows: 5003, 5134, 5265 and 5396 each expand outward and pale out under stress, and 5265's stress frame is a large empty hexagon while its neutral is a small dense one. Meanwhile neutral and recovery are nearly indistinguishable - 5396 neutral against 5396 recovery differs only in a slight brightness shift, and would be identical at 120px.
findings.why: The brief states the figure opens out in recovery and draws in under stress, carried by geometry rather than by weight. This runs the mapping backwards, and it carries the change largely by weight anyway - the filled core vanishing and everything going pale grey. It also spends the entire amplitude on one pairing, leaving the neutral-to-recovery comparison a viewer makes most often effectively dead.
findings.specificChange: Swap the direction of the extent mapping so recovery is the maximum reach and stress draws the outermost generations inward toward the centre, and widen the neutral-to-recovery extent delta until it is at least as large as the current neutral-to-stress delta, so all three states separate on reach alone.
findings.keep: The amplitude already present in the neutral-to-stress pairing - it survives to 120px, which is the expensive part. Redirect it, do not shrink it. And keep the token recognisably itself across all three states: symmetry order, member count and centre position must not change with market state, only extent.

findings.whatFails: On the 120px sheet eight of twelve seeds read as the same object: a dark core with a bone ring at roughly the same radius, sitting on an identical background, with the same faint blue-slate outer circle at nearly the same radius. Six-fold hexagonal symmetry dominates - 5265, 5527, 5920, 6313, 6444 and 6051 all sit in one family - and the palette is byte-identical across all twelve, so nothing but the interior detail (which dissolves at 120px) separates them.
findings.why: The variation strategy names symmetry as the FIRST axis tokens differ on, then reach, then fineness. Symmetry is barely moving, reach is nearly constant, and the fineness that does vary lives inside the dark core where it has no contrast to survive downscaling. The thumbnail intent asks that a fine radiating figure survive as a light silhouette - here twelve silhouettes are one silhouette.
findings.specificChange: Spread symmetry order across the seed space as the primary axis: pin each seed to a distinct fold count drawn from a wide set (4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12) instead of letting six-fold take eight of twelve, and increase per-seed variance in outermost extent so the 120px silhouettes differ in overall size as well as in fold count.
findings.keep: 5789's four-fold diamond and 6182's single wide ring with scattered satellites are the two tiles that already read as their own works - do not normalise them back toward the medallion while regularising the rest. Keep the shared bone-and-slate pairing and the shared dark ground as the identity anchors; the seeds should differ in geometry, not in colour.

overall: The generator is producing a competent centred recursive medallion, and the brief asked for something almost opposite to a medallion. The single largest gap is mass and value: every seed has a solid filled black core ringed by a thick bone band, sitting on a warm mid-value sepia vignette, which puts the darkest and heaviest element inside the artwork and the pale element in the ground - the exact inversion of bone and pale slate over a dark ground, and a direct contradiction of 'no filled mass anywhere'. Nothing here currently reads as hairline or fragile at any size. Second, the figure does not reach: it is a small object in a wide dead margin, generations do not thin as they go outward, and the one seed that does extend (6051) is clipped by the frame instead. Third, the market mapping runs backwards - stress expands and pales while recovery sits nearly on top of neutral - so the amplitude, which is genuinely strong and genuinely survives to 120px, is spent on the wrong pairing and in the wrong direction. Fourth, at browse size eight of twelve seeds are one seed, because six-fold symmetry dominates, extent barely varies, and the only real differentiation lives as fine detail inside a dark core where downscaling erases it. The recursion logic itself, the centring, the state amplitude, and the two sparse outliers (5789, 6182) are the assets to build from: unfill everything, invert the ground, push the outer generations out and thinner, reverse the market direction, and let symmetry order actually vary.
